- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.10) mid-horizon, model underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse — add 1–3% upward bias in next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates near-term (first 5–7 days) — reduce first 5 days by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.20+), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before next period.
